beur-hagra/1:א: (א) Who etc. makes kiddush. As was stated Berachos 39b: two times beloved etc. And even though the Mishnah changed the order, there is no need for it here; and see Tosafos 101 s.v. R' Yehuda.
beur-hagra/1:ב: (ב) That he blesses etc. There 114a, and in Beitzah he blesses etc., and the same applies to bread where there is wine; and there, in the Gemara because etc. another matter etc., and these reasons apply also to bread.
beur-hagra/1:ג: (ג) And he breaks. And specifically here, where he blesses on the piece; but on Shabbos and Yom Tov afterward not, as Rashbam wrote 39b s.v. beloved etc.; also he should not break etc., and Magen Avraham.
beur-hagra/1:ד: (ד) and resting. It is like a cup in a cup that is called a bad one
beur-hagra/1:ה: (ה) And he blesses etc. For those reasons do not apply; and on the contrary, here the reasons of Beit Shammai apply, and kiddush is also more frequent than matzah.
beur-hagra/1:ו: (ו) And afterward he eats. For before matzah it is impossible — it is forbidden to taste before kiddush.
beur-hagra/1:ז: (ז) And he removes etc. gaal yisrael. To exclude from Ra'ah, who wrote one does not bless gaal yisrael, which was only enacted on the cup; and it is not so, as was written there 117b: we learn in the Gemara etc. four cups etc., each one etc.
beur-hagra/1:ח: (ח) And you are blessed and then. We will not only repair the fairytale as if he had wine and assimilation at the time when he was adopted, and even the blessing of the bride would be worthy to welcome here only as another “catch” that Chris had served as “
beur-hagra/1:ט: (ט) Without a blessing. R. A.C. (J.A.A.A.C.) ceased the blessing of the West Bank and the people of Israel:
beur-hagra/1:י: (י) And in places etc. and some say etc. and it appears to me. As was written there 11 etc. and some say etc.; and for Rosh etc., since it is impossible in another matter — and this is what is written here; and it appears to me, since it is impossible to fulfill four cups, nevertheless.
chok-yaakov/1:א: (א) He who has no wine. A. D. D. D. D. A. D. has no wine or vows not to drink alcohol in the water of the thorns if they have a slump when they are arrested in the water. See the column that you need to bother to spend a lot of expenses to buy wine as it is committed to returning to the pancreas and squares and to the sign of the Renjo:
chok-yaakov/1:ב: (ב) Temple on the map. And he wrote in the Middle East that he does not have but one cup will take it to an end, and if he has years, he will take them to the food and blessing, and if he has a drink, he will make them three cups of the first, and if he has only two cups of licks of a glass on the night of two as a symbol of a sign:
chok-yaakov/1:ג: (ג) And he breaks. That is, he separates first the middle [matzah] and takes half for afikoman as above siman 473 and siman 475; and so too Magen Avraham.
chok-yaakov/1:ד: (ד) Until gaal yisrael. But Yehalelucha he does not say in the conclusion to praise, for it was enacted on the cup; and that which we say gaal yisrael is because it is in place of where He performed miracles, as was written siman 473 s.k. 2; and see Magen Avraham.
chok-yaakov/1:ה: (ה) That they are accustomed to drink. It implies specifically in a place where they are accustomed to drink it — then it is chamar medinah; and as the Rav concludes explicitly if it is chamar medinah; and also Bach's intent is as the Rav ruled in Shulchan Aruch, and it is simple; and not like Magen Avraham, who wrote that even if all year they are not accustomed to drink, nevertheless since they drink from it on Pesach it is called chamar medinah — and the main foundation of his words is from Bach's words; but in truth Bach agrees explicitly with the Rav's view here; and if so there is no foundation to his words at all, and one should not be lenient more than the Rav was lenient here end of his words.
